content_html:
The adhkar after salah (the remembrances said after the obligatory prayer) begin with seeking forgiveness three times and saying "Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta dhal-jalali wal-ikram". Then come the declarations of tawhid (that there is no god but Allah), then tasbih (SubhanAllah), tahmid (Alhamdulillah) and takbir (Allahu Akbar) thirty-three times each with a phrase that completes the hundred, then Ayat al-Kursi and the three protective surahs. It takes about five minutes after each fard prayer, and every remembrance in it is established in the Sunnah.

Below: each dhikr with its text, source, grading and meaning, other authentic forms of tasbih, what is specific to Fajr and Maghrib, and common mistakes.

What are the adhkar after salah in order?

  1. Say "Astaghfirullah" (I seek Allah's forgiveness) three times, then: "Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta dhal-jalali wal-ikram".
  2. "La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah... Allahumma la mani'a lima a'tayt, wa la mu'tiya lima mana't..."
  3. "La ilaha illallahu wahdah... la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah... wa law karihal-kafirun".
  4. SubhanAllah 33, Alhamdulillah 33, Allahu Akbar 33, then complete the hundred with "La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah...".
  5. Ayat al-Kursi (Quran 2:255).
  6. Surah Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas.
  7. "Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik".

This order follows many scholars and books such as Hisn al-Muslim (Fortress of the Muslim). Only the beginning is fixed by the text: istighfar and "Allahumma antas-salam" were the first things the Prophet ﷺ said after his prayer; the rest may come in any order.

Their basis is Allah's saying:

﴿فَإِذَا قَضَيْتُمُ الصَّلَاةَ فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ قِيَامًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِكُمْ﴾

"And when you have completed the prayer, remember Allah standing, sitting, or [lying] on your sides." (Surah An-Nisa 4:103, translation: Sahih International)

And His words: ﴿وَمِنَ اللَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَأَدْبَارَ السُّجُودِ﴾ "And [in part] of the night exalt Him and after prostration." (Surah Qaf 50:40, translation: Sahih International). Many commentators of the Quran explain "after prostration" as glorifying Allah after the prayers.

What is the text and source of each dhikr after salah?

1. Istighfar three times and "Allahumma antas-salam"

Thawban (may Allah be pleased with him) said that when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ finished his prayer, he would seek forgiveness three times and say:

«اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ السَّلَامُ، وَمِنْكَ السَّلَامُ، تَبَارَكْتَ ذَا الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ»

Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta dhal-jalali wal-ikram.

"O Allah, You are As-Salam (Peace) and from You comes peace. Blessed are You, Possessor of majesty and honour."

Al-Walid, one of the narrators, said: I asked al-Awza'i, "How is the forgiveness to be sought?" He said: "You say: Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah." (Sahih Muslim 591)

Meaning: you seek forgiveness straight after the prayer, since no servant's prayer is free of shortcomings, then praise Allah by His name As-Salam, the One free of every imperfection, from whom alone safety is sought. The wording in Thawban's narration is "tabarakta dhal-jalali", while in the narration of 'A'ishah in Muslim (592) it is "tabarakta ya dhal-jalali wal-ikram", and both are correct. For other forms of istighfar, see our article on Sayyid al-Istighfar.

2. "Allahumma la mani'a lima a'tayt"

Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah (may Allah be pleased with him) wrote to Mu'awiyah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet ﷺ used to say at the end of every obligatory prayer:

«لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، اللَّهُمَّ لَا مَانِعَ لِمَا أَعْطَيْتَ، وَلَا مُعْطِيَ لِمَا مَنَعْتَ، وَلَا يَنْفَعُ ذَا الْجَدِّ مِنْكَ الْجَدُّ»

La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. Allahumma la mani'a lima a'tayt, wa la mu'tiya lima mana't, wa la yanfa'u dhal-jaddi minkal-jadd.

"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. O Allah, none can withhold what You give, none can give what You withhold, and the wealth of the wealthy is of no avail against You." (Agreed upon: Sahih al-Bukhari 844 and Sahih Muslim 593)

Meaning: al-jadd means fortune, wealth and status. Wealth and position avail nothing before Allah; only righteous deeds do. The narrations in al-Bukhari and Muslim do not mention repeating it three times, so saying it once is enough.

3. The tahlil of Ibn az-Zubayr

'Abdullah ibn az-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with them both) used to say at the end of every prayer when he gave the salam:

«لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ، لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ، وَلَا نَعْبُدُ إِلَّا إِيَّاهُ، لَهُ النِّعْمَةُ وَلَهُ الْفَضْلُ وَلَهُ الثَّنَاءُ الْحَسَنُ، لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ وَلَوْ كَرِهَ الْكَافِرُونَ»

La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir. La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. La ilaha illallah, wa la na'budu illa iyyah, lahun-ni'matu wa lahul-fadlu wa lahuth-thana'ul-hasan. La ilaha illallahu mukhlisina lahud-dina wa law karihal-kafirun.

"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things. There is no might and no power except with Allah. There is no god but Allah, and we worship none but Him. His is the blessing, His is the bounty and His is the beautiful praise. There is no god but Allah; we make our religion sincerely His, even though the disbelievers dislike it."

And he said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to proclaim these at the end of every prayer." (Sahih Muslim 594)

Meaning: a renewal of tawhid after every prayer, a disowning of any might or power of your own, and an admission that every blessing and favour comes from Allah.

4. Tasbih, tahmid and takbir, completing the hundred

Abu Hurayrah narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever glorifies Allah at the end of every prayer thirty-three times, praises Allah thirty-three times and declares His greatness thirty-three times, that makes ninety-nine, and then completes the hundred by saying: La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamdu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir, his sins will be forgiven even if they are like the foam of the sea." (Sahih Muslim 597)

So you say SubhanAllah (Glory be to Allah), Alhamdulillah (All praise is for Allah) and Allahu Akbar (Allah is the Greatest) 33 times each, then the tahlil once. You may say them separately (SubhanAllah, SubhanAllah...) or together (SubhanAllah wal-hamdu lillah wallahu akbar) thirty-three times; both appear in the narrations.

5. Ayat al-Kursi

The Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever recites Ayat al-Kursi at the end of every obligatory prayer, nothing prevents him from entering Paradise except death." An-Nasa'i narrated it in as-Sunan al-Kubra (9848) from Abu Umamah, and al-Albani graded it sahih (authentic). Its text is verse 255 of Surah Al-Baqarah: ﴿اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ…﴾ "Allah - there is no deity except Him, the Ever-Living, the Self-Sustaining..." (Surah Al-Baqarah 2:255, translation: Sahih International).

6. The Mu'awwidhat

'Uqbah ibn 'Amir (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded me to recite the Mu'awwidhat at the end of every prayer." Abu Dawud (1523) and an-Nasa'i (1336) narrated it, and al-Albani graded it sahih. At-Tirmidhi (2903) narrated it with the wording "the two Mu'awwidhatayn" and called it gharib. The two Mu'awwidhatayn are Al-Falaq and An-Nas; many scholars, among them Ibn Hajar, included Al-Ikhlas under "Mu'awwidhat" by generalisation.

7. The advice to Mu'adh

Mu'adh ibn Jabal (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ took him by the hand and said: "O Mu'adh, by Allah, I love you." Then he said: "I advise you, O Mu'adh, never to leave saying at the end of every prayer:

«اللَّهُمَّ أَعِنِّي عَلَى ذِكْرِكَ وَشُكْرِكَ وَحُسْنِ عِبَادَتِكَ»

Allahumma a'inni 'ala dhikrika wa shukrika wa husni 'ibadatik.

"O Allah, help me to remember You, to thank You and to worship You well." (Narrated by Abu Dawud 1522 and an-Nasa'i; graded sahih by al-Albani)

Scholars differ on whether "the end of the prayer" here means before the salam, at the close of the tashahhud, or after it. The matter is broad, so say it in either place.

What are the other authentic forms of tasbih after salah?

Several forms of tasbih after the prayer are established from the Prophet ﷺ. The Sunnah is to vary between them or keep to one:

SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar + "La ilaha illallahu wahdah..." to complete the hundred33 / 33 / 33 / 1100Muslim 597

SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, La ilaha illallah, Allahu Akbar25 each100An-Nasa'i 1350 (sahih)
SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah, Allahu Akbar10 each30Al-Bukhari 6329

The second form is from Ka'b ibn 'Ujrah: "Follow-up phrases whose sayer is never disappointed at the end of every obligatory prayer: thirty-three tasbihah, thirty-three tahmidah and thirty-four takbirah." (Sahih Muslim 596). The third is from Zayd ibn Thabit: a man of the Ansar saw in a dream someone saying, "Make them twenty-five each and include the tahlil," and the Prophet ﷺ approved it (an-Nasa'i 1350, graded sahih by al-Albani). The fourth is in the hadith of the poor Muhajirun in al-Bukhari (6329) with "ten times", while other narrations of it say "thirty-three". The short form suits someone in a genuine hurry, so he does not leave the dhikr altogether.

Which adhkar are specific to Fajr and Maghrib?

The tahlil ten times after Fajr

Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Whoever says at the end of the Fajr prayer, while his legs are still folded and before he speaks:

«لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ المُلْكُ وَلَهُ الحَمْدُ، يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ، وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ»

La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah, lahul-mulku wa lahul-hamd, yuhyi wa yumit, wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadir.

"There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise. He gives life and causes death, and He has power over all things."

"...ten times," Allah writes for him ten good deeds, erases ten bad deeds from him, raises him ten degrees, and his day is spent in protection from Shaytan. At-Tirmidhi narrated it (3474) and said: hasan gharib sahih. Some hadith scholars have criticised its chain, while others strengthened it through supporting narrations, and some narrations mention Maghrib along with Fajr. "While his legs are still folded" means before leaving his tashahhud sitting position.

A du'a after the salam of Fajr

Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated that when the Prophet ﷺ prayed Fajr, he would say when he gave the salam:

«اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ عِلْمًا نَافِعًا، وَرِزْقًا طَيِّبًا، وَعَمَلًا مُتَقَبَّلًا»

Allahumma inni as'aluka 'ilman nafi'a, wa rizqan tayyiba, wa 'amalan mutaqabbala.

"O Allah, I ask You for beneficial knowledge, good provision and accepted deeds." (Ibn Majah 925; graded sahih by al-Albani)

A comprehensive du'a to begin your day.

The Mu'awwidhat three times after Fajr and Maghrib

The Mu'awwidhat are recited once after every prayer; some scholars recommend three times after Fajr and Maghrib, as these coincide with the morning and evening adhkar, which include them three times, so one recitation covers both. See our article on the virtues of the morning and evening adhkar.

"Allahumma ajirni minan-nar" seven times

It is widespread to say "Allahumma ajirni minan-nar" (O Allah, protect me from the Fire) seven times after Fajr and Maghrib. Its hadith was narrated by Abu Dawud (5079). Al-Albani graded it weak because one of its narrators is unknown, while some researchers graded it hasan. Whoever says it as a general du'a has done nothing wrong, but this number and its virtue should not be attributed to the Prophet ﷺ with certainty. See the details in this IslamQA fatwa (Arabic).

Should the adhkar come before or after the sunnah prayer?

The Prophet ﷺ said the adhkar straight after the obligatory prayer, so many scholars hold it is better to say the adhkar first and then pray the regular sunnah (rawatib). If you pray the sunnah first for a need and then say the adhkar, many scholars hold you do not lose their reward as long as the gap is short. If you must leave your place, say them wherever you are.

For making up a missed prayer, see what to do if you missed Fajr.

What are the common mistakes in the adhkar after salah?

1. Group dhikr in one voice

Scholars differ about raising the voice with dhikr after the prayer, based on the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "Raising the voice with dhikr when people finished the obligatory prayer was practised in the time of the Prophet ﷺ." He said: "I used to know when they had finished by hearing it." (Agreed upon: al-Bukhari 841 and Muslim 583)

  • The first view: saying dhikr quietly is better, and the loud dhikr in the hadith was to teach people and was later left. Ibn Rajab reported that this is the view of most scholars, and it is the known position of ash-Shafi'i.
  • The second view: raising the voice moderately is Sunnah, taking the hadith at its apparent meaning. This is the view of Ibn Baz and other contemporary scholars, on condition that it does not disturb those completing their prayer. See Ibn Baz's fatwa on raising the voice with dhikr after the prayer (Arabic).

As for worshippers reciting the dhikr in one organised voice like a choir, many scholars from both camps consider it an innovation that did not exist in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, because the apparent meaning of Ibn 'Abbas's hadith is that each person was remembering Allah on his own. Mosque customs differ between countries, so avoid arguing over it and hold to what unites.

2. Disturbing latecomers

Even according to those who allow saying it aloud, the voice must not rise to the point of distracting someone who is completing the part of the prayer he missed.

3. Rushing off and leaving all the adhkar

If you are in a hurry, do not leave the dhikr completely: say the istighfar, "Allahumma antas-salam", the tasbih ten times each and Ayat al-Kursi. It takes under two minutes.

4. Believing in a virtue that is not established

An example is placing the hand on the forehead after the salam while saying "Allahumma adhhib 'annil-hamma wal-hazan" (O Allah, remove from me worry and grief). Its hadith is very weak according to hadith scholars, and some judged it fabricated.

5. Counting without focus

Counting the tasbih on the fingers is the Sunnah. 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr (may Allah be pleased with them both) said: "I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ counting the tasbih (on his fingers)." (Abu Dawud 1502 and at-Tirmidhi 3486; graded sahih by al-Albani). Using a misbaha (prayer beads) or a counter to keep count is fine according to many scholars. What matters is a present heart.

How can I memorise the adhkar after salah and keep them up?

  1. Memorise them one at a time: begin with the istighfar, "Allahumma antas-salam" and the tasbih, the easiest.
  2. Add one dhikr each week: the first tahlil, then the second, then Ayat al-Kursi, then the advice to Mu'adh.
  3. Tie them to your place: stay in your prayer spot until you finish.
  4. Train your children: have your child do the tasbih with you on their fingers after prayers at home. Our article on daily adhkar for kids has a plan suited to their ages.
  5. Track yourself: log your adhkar alongside your prayers in the daily worship tracker.

It has no ads, needs no account, and is coming soon to Google Play.

Summary

The adhkar after salah are five minutes that guard your prayer's reward: istighfar three times, "Allahumma antas-salam", the tahlil, tasbih in one of the established forms, Ayat al-Kursi, the Mu'awwidhat and the advice to Mu'adh. Fajr adds the tahlil ten times and the du'a for "beneficial knowledge". Saying dhikr aloud is a valid difference of opinion, so do not let it cause disputes. This is a summary of scholars' views; for your own situation, ask trusted scholars in your country.

faq.q: How many times do I say Astaghfirullah after salah?
faq.a: Three times, then you say: Allahumma antas-salam wa minkas-salam, tabarakta dhal-jalali wal-ikram, as in the hadith of Thawban in Sahih Muslim (591). Al-Awza'i, one of the narrators, was asked how to seek forgiveness and said: you say Astaghfirullah, Astaghfirullah. So no longer wording is required.

faq.q: Is the takbir after salah 33 or 34 times?
faq.a: Both are established. In Sahih Muslim (597) the tasbih, tahmid and takbir are thirty-three each, then the hundred is completed with La ilaha illallahu wahdahu la sharika lah. In Sahih Muslim (596) the takbir is thirty-four, without the tahlil. So use one form at one time and the other at another, or keep to one of them.

faq.q: Are the Mu'awwidhat recited once or three times after each prayer?
faq.a: They are recited once after every prayer, based on the hadith of 'Uqbah ibn 'Amir in Abu Dawud (1523). Some scholars consider it recommended to recite them three times after Fajr and Maghrib, because these coincide with the morning and evening adhkar, in which Al-Ikhlas and the two Mu'awwidhatayn are recited three times, so one recitation covers both.

faq.q: Is it allowed to say dhikr aloud after salah?
faq.a: There is a valid difference of opinion. Most scholars hold that saying it quietly is better and that saying it aloud was for teaching, while others, including Ibn Baz, hold that raising it moderately is Sunnah, based on the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas in al-Bukhari and Muslim, as long as it does not disturb others praying. Group dhikr in one voice is considered not legislated by many scholars.

faq.q: Do I say the adhkar before or after the sunnah prayer?
faq.a: Many scholars consider it better to say the adhkar straight after the obligatory prayer and then pray the sunnah, because the adhkar are tied to the end of the prayer. If you pray the sunnah first for a need and then say the adhkar a short while later, many scholars see no harm in that. The important thing is not to leave them.

faq.q: What if I forgot the adhkar after salah and left my place?
faq.a: Say them when you remember, as long as it is still close to the prayer, even if you are walking or somewhere else, since dhikr does not require a particular place. If a long time has passed, remember Allah with general dhikr, for Allah does not let the reward of good deeds be lost, and at the next prayer try not to get up until you have finished.
